questionText: A patient with known coronary disease reports increased fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and weakness. SpO₂ is 98% on room air, but hemoglobin is significantly below the patient’s baseline. No ECG or troponin results are available yet. Select ONE best-supported condition, TWO nursing actions, and TWO parameters.
rationale: Normal SpO₂ does not exclude anemia because saturation does not measure the amount of hemoglobin available to carry oxygen. Anemia may worsen fatigue, dyspnea, and angina, but it should not automatically be assumed to explain all new symptoms in a patient with coronary disease. Trend CBC and clinical/ischemic findings.

questionText: A patient with CKD has hs-troponin above the assay’s 99th-percentile reference limit, but the first value is the only result available. The patient denies chest discomfort; baseline dyspnea is unchanged, and no ECG interpretation is yet available. Select ONE best interpretation, TWO actions, and TWO parameters.
rationale: Troponin above the assay-specific 99th percentile indicates myocardial injury but does not automatically prove acute MI. A rise/fall and evidence of ischemia are needed for MI interpretation. Use serial results, ECG, symptoms, kidney function, and clinical context; neither absent chest pain nor a single elevated value should end the evaluation.
